sections.content: How many people are "library clerks and assistants"?

18,740 people

were counted on the census as "library clerks and assistants" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Library clerks and assistants classify, sort and file publications, documents, audio-visual and computerised material in libraries and offices.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "library clerks and assistants" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "library clerks and assistants", 16.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "library clerks and assistants" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "library clerks and assistants" included:

  • gardeners and landscape gardeners
  • roundspersons and van salespersons
  • glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "library clerks and assistants" there were more women than men (76.6% compared with 23.4%).

This means "library clerks and assistants" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 23.4% and women made up 76.6% of "library clerks and assistants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "library clerks and assistants" included:

  • social services managers and directors
  • other health professionals
  • other educational professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "library clerks and assistants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "library clerks and assistants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "library clerks and assistants", 18.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (62.1% compared with 37.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (99%) than self-employed (1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
